_comment: EXP-93. The mix-shift stress trace. Same hour, same arrival band 10-45 req/s,
same seed, and the SAME ARRIVAL TIMES as mix_dyn60_short_m123_b1045.json --
the two plan CSVs are byte-identical in the arrival_s column and differ only
in the class label of 46,632 of the 99,242 rows. Only the mix schedule moved,
so any difference between a run on this trace and a run on that one is
attributable to the class mix and not to the arrival process.
Mix schedule m2,A,m1,B instead of m1,m2,m3,m1, by request count:
s0 m2  chat 93.0 / deepresearch  4.7 / swe  2.3 %
s1 A   chat 33.3 / deepresearch 33.3 / swe 33.3 %   <- the even region
s2 m1  chat 76.9 / deepresearch 15.4 / swe  7.7 %
s3 B   chat 60.0 / deepresearch 30.0 / swe 10.0 %
Why. The deployed hour trace moves chat between 66.7% and 93.0% of the
requests and never approaches an even mix, so the claim that the system is
robust to a shift in the class mix is currently supported only inside a
chat-majority region. This schedule reaches 33.3% and steps in both
directions (93.0 -> 33.3 -> 76.9 -> 60.0), which widens the measured shift
and tests recovery rather than only degradation.
What the shift does to capacity, which is the point of the experiment: the
arrival band is unchanged while the workload's weight per request is not.
Mean input tokens per request, derived from the class means (chat 674,
deepresearch 4,055, swe 6,812), are about 970 in s0 and about 3,850 in s1, a
factor of four, and FluidServe v0.2's 90% knee is 28.0 req/s on m1 against an
estimated 12.5 req/s on the even mix (extrapolated from EXP-92's two rates,
15 and 20 req/s, so it is an estimate and not a measurement). The arrival
rate therefore crosses a knee that the arrival rate itself did not move.
KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded rather than fixed. The swe transcript holds 1,500
records. On m1 the class is 1/13 of the arrivals, so a record returns every
9.1 minutes, which is longer than both the engine's prompt residence (about 1
minute) and the scheduler's prefix index (about 2.8 minutes). In the s1
segment the class is 1/3 of the arrivals and a record returns about every 2.7
minutes, which is inside the scheduler's prefix index, so swe's prefix hit
rate is inflated in that segment. Both arms see the same trace, but they
exploit prefix reuse through different mechanisms, so the segment-1 numbers
are not a clean comparison of prefix behaviour. Enlarging the transcript is a
separate open task and would trade this for a worse problem (a 13,218-record
build has 98.9% structural prefix sharing against this sample's 78.9%).
Derived from mix_dyn60_short_m123_b1045.json; only class_plan_file changed.
